correctness.rationale: For any all-positive two-cycle with x0<x1, set s=x1/x0>1. The exact prey updates force x0+y0=2-s and x1+y1=2-1/s, hence y1-y0=(s-1)(1+1/s-x0)>0 since x0<2-s<1. Predator multipliers t0=1-r+gamma*x0 and t1=1-r+gamma*x1 are positive with t0*t1=1 and t0<t1, hence t0<1, y1<y0, contradiction. Equal-x case is fixed; invariant coordinate axes admit only fixed nonnegative two-step states. Fixed-point equations give exactly stated census; no whole-quadrant invariance was assumed. Inspected exact symbolic script and independent identity derivation; finite grid is corroboration only.

value.rationale: Global absence of the first possible nonfixed periodic behavior over all positive r,gamma in an ecologically motivated discrete model is a structural dynamical obstruction, not an axis-only check. It remains informative above a Neimark–Sacker threshold and outside previously proved invariant-triangle basins; restrictions and future higher-period questions are explicit.

final_claim: For every r>0 and gamma>0, F(x,y)=(x(2-x-y), y(1-r+gamma*x)) has no nonfixed prime-two orbit with both states nonnegative. Its period<=2 nonnegative census contains only (0,0),(1,0), and, if gamma>r, (r/gamma,1-r/gamma).
limitations: Requires BOTH states of a period-two orbit to stay nonnegative and r,gamma>0. Does not prove global quadrant invariance, absence of higher periods, or global convergence.
